title: Coordinates of a Point on a Square Root Curve as Functions of Secant Slope
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: A point P in the first quadrant lies on the graph of the function f(x) = sqrt(x). Express the coordinates of P as functions of the slope m of the line joining P to the origin.

steps.title: Represent Point P and the Slope m to the Origin
steps.explanation: Since P lies on f(x) = sqrt(x) in the first quadrant, its coordinates are (x, sqrt(x)) with x > 0. The slope m of the line through (0, 0) and (x, sqrt(x)) is sqrt(x)/x = 1/sqrt(x).
steps.why: The slope of a line passing through the origin and (x, y) is m = y / x.

steps.title: Solve for the x-Coordinate in Terms of m
steps.explanation: Take the reciprocal of m = 1/sqrt(x) to get sqrt(x) = 1/m, and square both sides to express x as a function of m: x(m) = 1/m^2.
steps.why: Squaring both sides of a positive equality preserves equivalence.

steps.title: Find the y-Coordinate in Terms of m
steps.explanation: Since y = sqrt(x) and we already found sqrt(x) = 1/m (with m > 0 in the first quadrant), the y-coordinate of P is y(m) = 1/m. Thus P = (1/m^2, 1/m).
steps.why: Substituting sqrt(x) = 1/m directly gives the ordinate y on the curve y = sqrt(x).
